proof.claim:
Surface the release pipeline state as known, documented cluster state.

What this scenario asserts:
  - The release audit probe works and returns a parseable result
  - Total ServiceRelease count is above a minimum (proves records exist)
  - Releases actually converge — at least one reaches a terminal success
    phase, proving the pipeline is not permanently stuck

History (2026-08-11): this scenario previously asserted the OPPOSITE —
failed_gte matching the total, and succeeded == 0 — on the stated premise
that "all ServiceRelease records are in FAILED phase" because of stale MinIO
credentials. That premise was largely an artifact of the audit probe itself:
it counted phase == "SUCCEEDED", a phase that does not exist in the release
vocabulary (see ReleasePhase* in cluster_controllerpb/resources_types.go —
the terminal success phase is AVAILABLE). Every converged release was
therefore invisible to the probe and filed under "pending", making a working
pipeline look permanently broken. With the probe reading the real phases, the
cluster shows converged releases alongside a small number of genuine
failures.

Deliberately NOT asserted: an exact failure count. This scenario runs after
the chaos suites, which legitimately leave some releases FAILED; pinning a
number is what made the previous version break the moment the system
improved.

authority.note: Simulation output is evidence/candidate knowledge only. Governed promotion is required before production may rely on it.
